EN.C8_pressure: Ten minutes. Check the bleeding. Still bleeding? Keep pressing.
EN.C8_nosebleed: Ten minutes. Release slowly. Still bleeding? Pinch ten more.
EN.C9: Tourniquet on for N minutes. Do not loosen.
EN.speaker: Tap SPEAKER on the call screen. Phone asks to unlock? Use EMERGENCY CALL.

TL.C4: Magpalit ng magdi-diin. Tingnan ang paghinga.
TL.C8_pressure: Sampung minuto na. Dumudugo pa? Ituloy ang diin.
TL.C8_nosebleed: Sampung minuto na. Dumudugo pa? Ipitin ulit nang sampung minuto.
TL.C9: Naka-tourniquet na nang N minuto. Huwag luwagan.
TL.C10: Lagpas limang minuto na. Tumawag sa 911 ngayon.
TL.speaker: Pindutin ang SPEAKER sa call screen. Pinapa-unlock? Gamitin ang EMERGENCY CALL.

quiz.q: Blood is spurting from a thigh wound. What do you do first?
options: Press hard on the wound with cloth
Raise the leg above the heart
quiz.why: Firm direct pressure is the first and fastest way to stop heavy bleeding.
quiz.qTl: Bumubulwak ang dugo sa sugat sa hita. Ano ang una mong gagawin?
optionsTl: Diinan nang malakas ang sugat gamit ang tela
Itaas ang binti lampas sa puso
quiz.whyTl: Ang matibay na diin ang una at pinakamabilis na paraan para pigilan ang malakas na pagdurugo.

quiz.q: With plain cloth, how long should you keep firm pressure before checking?
quiz.why: Plain cloth needs about 10 minutes for a clot to form; 3 minutes is only for hemostatic gauze.
quiz.qTl: Kung ordinaryong tela, gaano katagal didiinan bago silipin?
quiz.whyTl: Kailangan ng mga 10 minuto ang ordinaryong tela para mamuo ang dugo; ang 3 minuto ay para lang sa hemostatic gauze.

quiz.q: Blood soaks through the cloth you are pressing. What now?
options: Remove it and use a fresh one
Stop pressing and tie a string
Add more cloth on top and keep pressing
quiz.why: Removing the first layer pulls off the clot and restarts the bleeding.
quiz.qTl: Tumatagos ang dugo sa telang idinidiin mo. Ano ngayon?
optionsTl: Itigil ang diin at talian ng pisi
Patungan pa ng tela at ituloy ang diin
quiz.whyTl: Ang pagtanggal sa unang tela ay humihila sa namuong dugo at nagpapadugo ulit.

quiz.q: You must improvise a tourniquet. Which is correct?
options: Use a pen as the twist stick
Place it on the elbow joint
Use a wide band 5–7 cm above the wound, twist with a strong stick
quiz.why: A wide band above the wound with a strong stick works; pens snap, joints block pressure, and loosening can kill.
quiz.qTl: Kailangan mong gumawa ng tourniquet. Alin ang tama?
optionsTl: Malapad na tali 5–7 cm sa itaas ng sugat, pihitin gamit ang matibay na patpat
quiz.whyTl: Gumagana ang malapad na tali sa itaas ng sugat at matibay na patpat; nababali ang ballpen, hinaharangan ng kasukasuan ang diin, at nakamamatay ang pagluwag.

quiz.q: Someone collapsed and is only gasping. What does that mean?
options: They are breathing, wait and watch
Treat as not breathing: call 911 and start CPR
Put them in the recovery position and leave
quiz.why: Gasping is not normal breathing; it's a sign of cardiac arrest.
quiz.qTl: May bumagsak at humihingal lang. Ano ang ibig sabihin nito?
optionsTl: Ituring na hindi humihinga: tumawag sa 911 at mag-CPR
quiz.whyTl: Ang paghingal ay hindi normal na paghinga; senyales ito ng cardiac arrest.

quiz.q: How deep and how fast are adult chest compressions?
quiz.why: 5–6 cm at 100–120 per minute moves enough blood; ARCHER beeps at 110.
quiz.qTl: Gaano kalalim at kabilis ang pagdiin sa dibdib ng adult?
quiz.whyTl: Ang 5–6 cm sa 100–120 kada minuto ay sapat na nagpapadaloy ng dugo; 110 ang tunog ng ARCHER.

quiz.q: You are not trained in rescue breaths. What CPR should you do?
quiz.why: Hands-only CPR by an untrained bystander still doubles survival chances.
quiz.qTl: Hindi ka trained sa rescue breath. Anong CPR ang gagawin mo?
quiz.whyTl: Malaki pa rin ang naitutulong ng hands-only CPR ng hindi trained na tumutulong.

quiz.q: An AED arrives during CPR. What do you do?
options: Finish 10 more minutes of CPR first
Turn it on and follow its voice; keep pushing until it says stop
Only use it if you are a nurse
Use it after drying the person for 5 minutes
quiz.why: AEDs are made for anyone; the voice guides you and a shock can restart the heart.
quiz.qTl: Dumating ang AED habang nagsi-CPR. Ano ang gagawin mo?
optionsTl: Buksan at sundin ang boses nito; ituloy ang diin hanggang sabihing tumigil
Gamitin pagkatapos patuyuin ang tao nang 5 minuto
quiz.whyTl: Para sa lahat ang AED; gagabayan ka ng boses at puwedeng ibalik ng shock ang tibok ng puso.

quiz.q: An adult can't speak or cough, hands on throat. What is the first action?
options: 5 hard back blows, then 5 abdominal thrusts
Sweep the throat with your finger
quiz.why: Back blows then abdominal thrusts, repeated, is the current guidance for severe choking.
quiz.qTl: Hindi makapagsalita o makaubo ang adult, hawak ang lalamunan. Ano ang unang gagawin?
optionsTl: 5 malakas na palo sa likod, saka 5 tulak sa tiyan
quiz.whyTl: Ang palo sa likod at tulak sa tiyan, paulit-ulit, ang kasalukuyang gabay sa matinding pagkabulon.

quiz.q: A baby under 1 year is choking and can't cry. What do you do?
options: 5 back blows, then 5 chest thrusts with the heel of one hand
Give milk to wash it down
quiz.why: Babies get back blows and chest thrusts; belly thrusts can injure a baby's organs.
quiz.qTl: Nabulunan ang sanggol na wala pang 1 taon at hindi makaiyak. Ano ang gagawin mo?
optionsTl: Itulak ang tiyan gaya ng adult
5 palo sa likod, saka 5 diin sa dibdib gamit ang palad ng isang kamay
quiz.whyTl: Palo sa likod at diin sa dibdib para sa sanggol; puwedeng makasakit ng laman-loob ang tulak sa tiyan.

quiz.q: The choking person collapses and stops responding. Next step?
options: Lower them down, call 911, start CPR
quiz.why: Chest compressions also push on the blockage; check the mouth before any breaths.
quiz.qTl: Bumagsak at hindi na tumutugon ang nabulunan. Ano ang susunod?
optionsTl: Ituloy ang tulak sa tiyan nang nakatayo
Ihiga, tumawag sa 911, simulan ang CPR
quiz.whyTl: Ang pagdiin sa dibdib ay tumutulak din sa bara; silipin ang bibig bago magbigay ng hininga.

quiz.q: How long should you cool a burn under clean running water?
quiz.why: 20 minutes of cool running water stops the burn going deeper and eases pain.
quiz.qTl: Gaano katagal palalamigin ang paso sa malinis na umaagos na tubig?
quiz.whyTl: Ang 20 minutong umaagos na tubig ay pumipigil sa paglalim ng paso at nagpapagaan ng sakit.

quiz.q: What should you put on a burn after cooling?
options: Loose cling wrap or a clean plastic bag
quiz.why: Cling wrap keeps germs out and doesn't stick; the others trap heat or damage skin.
quiz.qTl: Ano ang ilalagay sa paso pagkatapos palamigin?
optionsTl: Maluwag na cling wrap o malinis na plastik
quiz.whyTl: Hinaharangan ng cling wrap ang mikrobyo at hindi dumidikit; ang iba ay nagkukulong ng init o sumisira ng balat.

quiz.q: A guard on duty is confused, very hot, and collapsed. What is the best cooling?
options: Cold water up to the neck (or soak and fan) and call 911
Let them rest in the sun
quiz.why: This is heat stroke: call 911 and cool fast; cold-water immersion is the fastest method.
quiz.qTl: Lito, napakainit, at bumagsak ang guwardiya habang naka-duty. Ano ang pinakamahusay na pagpapalamig?
optionsTl: Ilubog sa malamig na tubig hanggang leeg (o basain at paypayan) at tumawag sa 911
quiz.whyTl: Heat stroke ito: tumawag sa 911 at palamigin agad; pinakamabilis ang paglubog sa malamig na tubig.

quiz.q: Heat exhaustion: alert, sweaty, dizzy. When do you treat it as heat stroke?
options: If not better in 30 minutes, or they get confused
quiz.why: Heat exhaustion can turn into heat stroke; confusion or no improvement means emergency.
quiz.qTl: Heat exhaustion: gising, pawisan, nahihilo. Kailan ito ituturing na heat stroke?
optionsTl: Kung hindi gumaling sa 30 minuto, o naging lito
quiz.whyTl: Puwedeng mauwi sa heat stroke ang heat exhaustion; emergency kapag lito o hindi gumagaling.

quiz.q: Someone is having a seizure. Which is correct?
options: Clear hard objects, cushion the head, time it
Put a spoon in their mouth
quiz.why: Protect from injury and time it; holding down or objects in the mouth cause injuries.
quiz.qTl: May nagkokombulsyon. Alin ang tama?
optionsTl: Ilayo ang matitigas na bagay, unanan ang ulo, orasan
quiz.whyTl: Protektahan sa pinsala at orasan; ang pagpigil o paglagay ng bagay sa bibig ay nagdudulot ng pinsala.

quiz.q: When is a seizure a 911 emergency?
options: Over 5 minutes, or another seizure follows
Never, seizures stop on their own
quiz.why: A seizure over 5 minutes risks brain injury and needs medicine fast.
quiz.qTl: Kailan emergency sa 911 ang kombulsyon?
optionsTl: Lagpas 5 minuto, o may sumunod pang kombulsyon
quiz.whyTl: Ang kombulsyong lagpas 5 minuto ay delikado sa utak at kailangan agad ng gamot.

quiz.q: When do you use the recovery position?
options: Unresponsive but breathing normally, no suspected spine injury
quiz.why: On the side keeps the airway open and lets vomit drain while they breathe.
quiz.qTl: Kailan gagamitin ang recovery position?
optionsTl: Walang malay pero normal na humihinga, walang hinalang pinsala sa gulugod
quiz.whyTl: Ang pagtagilid ay nagpapanatiling bukas ng daanan ng hangin at nagpapalabas ng suka habang humihinga siya.

quiz.q: After placing someone in the recovery position, what must you keep doing?
options: Leave to get help and don't come back
quiz.why: They can stop breathing without warning; if they do, start CPR.
quiz.qTl: Matapos i-recovery position, ano ang dapat mong ituloy?
optionsTl: Umalis para humingi ng tulong at huwag nang bumalik
quiz.whyTl: Puwede siyang tumigil huminga nang walang babala; kung mangyari, mag-CPR.

quiz.q: Many people are hurt after a blast. Who do you go to first?
options: Whoever is closest to the exit
quiz.why: Silent, still patients are often the most critical; walkers are lower priority.
quiz.qTl: Maraming sugatan pagkatapos ng pagsabog. Sino ang una mong pupuntahan?
quiz.whyTl: Kadalasang pinakamalala ang tahimik at hindi gumagalaw; mas mababa ang prayoridad ng nakakalakad.

quiz.q: You are alone with ONE patient who is not breathing. What do you do?
quiz.why: 'Move on' is only for mass casualties with many patients; one patient not breathing gets CPR.
quiz.qTl: Mag-isa ka at may ISANG pasyenteng hindi humihinga. Ano ang gagawin mo?
quiz.whyTl: Ang 'lumipat sa susunod' ay para lang sa maraming sugatan; ang isang pasyenteng hindi humihinga ay bibigyan ng CPR.

quiz.q: You see an injured person lying on a busy road. What is step zero?
options: Check the scene is safe: traffic, fire, wires, attacker
Move them off the road by the arms right away
quiz.why: A hurt rescuer can't help anyone; make the scene safe first.
quiz.qTl: May nakahigang sugatan sa mataong kalsada. Ano ang step zero?
optionsTl: Tingnan kung ligtas ang lugar: trapiko, sunog, kawad, umaatake
Hilahin agad sa braso palabas ng kalsada
quiz.whyTl: Walang matutulungan ang tumutulong na nasaktan; gawing ligtas muna ang lugar.

quiz.q: A worker is stuck to a power line that is down on the street. What do you do?
options: Pull him off with your hands
Push the wire with a wet stick
Stay 10 m away, keep others back, call 911 and the power company
quiz.why: High-voltage current can jump; never approach a downed line.
quiz.qTl: May trabahador na nakadikit sa bumagsak na kawad ng kuryente sa kalsada. Ano ang gagawin mo?
optionsTl: Itulak ang kawad ng basang patpat
Lumayo nang 10 metro, ilayo ang iba, tumawag sa 911 at sa kompanya ng kuryente
quiz.whyTl: Puwedeng tumalon ang high-voltage na kuryente; huwag lumapit sa bagsak na kawad.

quiz.q: What is the emergency number for police, fire and ambulance in the Philippines?
quiz.why: 911 is the national emergency hotline in the Philippines.
quiz.qTl: Ano ang emergency number para sa pulis, bumbero at ambulansya sa Pilipinas?
quiz.whyTl: 911 ang pambansang emergency hotline sa Pilipinas.

quiz.q: On the 911 call while doing CPR, what helps most?
options: Put the phone on speaker and give the exact location
Hang up so you can focus
quiz.why: Speaker lets the dispatcher coach you; an exact location saves minutes.
quiz.qTl: Habang tumatawag sa 911 at nagsi-CPR, ano ang pinakamakakatulong?
optionsTl: I-speaker ang telepono at sabihin ang eksaktong lokasyon
quiz.whyTl: Sa speaker, matuturuan ka ng dispatcher; nakakatipid ng minuto ang eksaktong lokasyon.

rules.sceneSafeWhy: traffic, fire, wires, an attacker or a crowd can turn you into patient number two.
rules.speakFirst: Call 911 now, or have someone call.
rules.speakFirstTl: Tumawag sa 911 ngayon, o magpatawag sa iba.
rules.sceneSafeDetail: CHECK SCENE SAFE: traffic, fire, wires, attacker, crowd. Don't become victim #2.
rules.gloves: Gloves: if none, use plastic bag, plastic wrapper, or clean cloth over your hand.
rules.footer: Not a substitute for professional care. Get medical help ASAP.
rules.trainingNote: Quick guide, not a replacement for proper first-aid training.
rules.cpr2minTl: Magpalit ng magdi-diin. Tingnan ang paghinga.
rules.basis: Based on standard lay-responder first aid guidance (Red Cross / AHA / Stop the Bleed style).

cards.title: Severe bleeding
signs: blood spurting or pooling, soaking through cloth, person getting pale/weak.
doNot: Don't lift to check.
Don't remove the first layer.
Never thin wire, string or cable tie.
Do NOT loosen.
Do NOT raise the legs after an injury or bleeding.
detail: Signs: blood spurting or pooling, soaking through cloth, person getting pale/weak.
1. Call 911. Protect your hands (bag/plastic).
2. PRESS HARD directly on the wound with cloth, both hands, full body weight. Don't lift to check. Keep pressing at least 10 minutes with plain cloth.
3. Blood soaks through? Add more cloth on top. Don't remove the first layer.
4. Deep wound (thigh, armpit, neck, groin)? PACK IT: stuff cloth deep into the wound with your fingers, then press hard for 10 minutes (3 minutes only if you have hemostatic gauze).
5. Arm or leg still bleeding badly after firm pressure? TOURNIQUET:
- Use a commercial (manufactured) tourniquet if you have one. It works best.
- No commercial tourniquet? Improvise only after firm direct pressure fails (best if trained).
- Band 4–5 cm wide (folded shirt, scarf, belt). Never thin wire, string or cable tie.
- Place 5–7 cm above the wound, not on a joint.
- Tie, put a strong stick on the knot (not a pen, it can snap), twist until bleeding STOPS, secure the stick.
- Write the time on the skin or forehead. Do NOT loosen.
6. Lay them down and keep them warm. Do NOT raise the legs after an injury or bleeding.
Nearby items: shirt, towel, face towel, sanitary pad, diaper, belt, necktie, strong stick, wrench or screwdriver as windlass, tape.
Sources: AHA/Red Cross First Aid Guidelines 2024; ERC Guidelines 2025 First Aid; Stop the Bleed (ACS).

steps.text: Check the scene is safe.
steps.tl: Siguraduhing ligtas ang lugar.
steps.why: a hurt rescuer can't help anyone.

steps.text: Cover your hands with plastic or cloth.
steps.tl: Takpan ang kamay ng plastik o tela.
steps.why: protects you from blood-borne infection.

steps.text: Press hard on the wound with cloth.
steps.tl: Diinan nang malakas ang sugat gamit ang tela.
steps.why: pressure squeezes the vessel shut so blood can clot.

steps.text: Use both hands and your body weight.
steps.tl: Gamitin ang dalawang kamay at bigat ng katawan.
steps.why: pressure squeezes the vessel shut so blood can clot.

steps.text: Do not lift the cloth to check.
steps.tl: Huwag iangat ang tela para silipin.
steps.why: lifting breaks the clot that's forming.

steps.text: Blood soaking through? Add more cloth on top.
steps.tl: Tumatagos ang dugo? Patungan pa ng tela.
steps.why: removing the first layer restarts bleeding.

steps.text: Deep wound? Stuff cloth into it, then press hard.
steps.tl: Malalim ang sugat? Isiksik ang tela, saka diinan.
steps.why: pressure has to reach the bleeding vessel inside.

steps.text: Keep pressing for at least ten minutes.
steps.tl: Diinan nang hindi bababa sa sampung minuto.
steps.why: plain cloth needs about 10 minutes of firm pressure for a clot to form; 3 minutes is only for hemostatic gauze.

steps.text: Still bleeding badly? Use a real tourniquet if you have one.
steps.tl: Malakas pa rin ang dugo? Gumamit ng tunay na tourniquet kung mayroon.
steps.why: stops blood flow to a limb when pressure fails; a real one works far better than an improvised one.

steps.text: No tourniquet? Make one with a wide band: shirt, scarf, belt.
steps.tl: Walang tourniquet? Gumawa gamit ang malapad na tali: damit, panyo, sinturon.
steps.why: thin cord cuts skin and doesn't compress evenly.

steps.text: Tie it a hand-width above the wound, not on a joint.
steps.tl: Itali isang dangkal sa itaas ng sugat, hindi sa kasukasuan.
steps.why: bones in joints block compression.

steps.text: Put a strong stick on the knot, not a pen.
steps.tl: Maglagay ng matibay na patpat sa buhol, hindi ballpen.
steps.why: a pen can snap mid-twist and the bleeding returns.

steps.text: Twist until the bleeding stops.
steps.tl: Pihitin hanggang tumigil ang dugo.
steps.why: a loose tourniquet can make bleeding worse.

steps.text: Tie the stick in place. Do not loosen.
steps.tl: Itali ang patpat. Huwag luwagan.
steps.why: releasing can cause sudden fatal blood loss.

steps.text: Write the time on their skin.
steps.tl: Isulat ang oras sa balat niya.
steps.why: doctors need to know how long blood was cut off.

steps.text: Lay them down and keep them warm.
steps.tl: Ihiga siya at panatilihing mainit.
steps.why: slows shock from blood loss; don't raise injured legs, it can worsen hidden injuries.

cards.title: Cuts and wounds
doNot: Do NOT pull out deeply stuck objects; pad around them.
detail: 1. Press with clean cloth until bleeding stops (about 5–10 min).
2. Rinse with clean running water (bottled/tap) for several minutes. No need for strong alcohol inside the wound.
3. Remove visible dirt by rinsing. Do NOT pull out deeply stuck objects; pad around them.
4. Cover with clean cloth or plaster. Change daily.
5. Get to a clinic if: gaping edges, deep, on face/hands/joints, from rusty metal or animal (tetanus/rabies shot), or signs of infection (red, hot, pus, fever).
Nearby items: bottled water, clean handkerchief, tissue + tape, sanitary pad, plastic wrap.
Sources: AHA/Red Cross First Aid Guidelines 2024; IFRC First Aid Guidelines.

steps.text: Press with clean cloth until bleeding stops.
steps.tl: Diinan ng malinis na tela hanggang tumigil ang dugo.
steps.why: most minor bleeding stops with pressure alone.

steps.text: Rinse with clean water for a few minutes.
steps.tl: Banlawan ng malinis na tubig nang ilang minuto.
steps.why: clean water removes dirt and lowers infection risk.

steps.text: Do not pull out deeply stuck objects.
steps.tl: Huwag hugutin ang nakabaong bagay.
steps.why: they may be plugging a bleeding vessel.

steps.text: Cover with clean cloth or a plaster.
steps.tl: Takpan ng malinis na tela o plaster.
steps.why: keeps germs out while it heals.

steps.text: Deep, gaping, or from an animal or rusty metal? See a doctor.
steps.tl: Malalim, nakabuka, o galing sa hayop o kalawang? Magpatingin sa doktor.
steps.why: may need rabies or tetanus shots.

cards.title: Road traffic accident
doNot: Do NOT move the injured unless there is fire, fuel leak, or traffic danger.
Do NOT remove a motorcycle helmet unless they are not breathing or vomiting.
detail: 1. Make the scene safe: hazard lights, warning triangle or bag/branches 30+ m behind, phone flashlight. Turn off engine if safe. No smoking.
2. Call 911. Give exact location (landmark, km post).
3. Do NOT move the injured unless there is fire, fuel leak, or traffic danger.
4. Do NOT remove a motorcycle helmet unless they are not breathing or vomiting.
5. Keep head and neck still: kneel behind and hold head in line with your hands.
6. Check breathing. Not breathing normally? Go to CARDIAC ARREST card.
7. Treat severe bleeding next (card 1). Keep warm, keep talking to them.
Nearby items: hazard lights, phone flashlight, jacket for warmth, rolled towels beside the head.
Sources: AHA/Red Cross First Aid Guidelines 2024; ERC Guidelines 2025 First Aid; IFRC First Aid Guidelines.

steps.text: Turn on hazard lights. Make the scene safe.
steps.tl: I-on ang hazard lights. Gawing ligtas ang lugar.
steps.why: secondary crashes injure rescuers.

steps.text: Put a warning sign thirty meters behind.
steps.tl: Maglagay ng babala tatlumpung metro sa likod.
steps.why: secondary crashes injure rescuers.

steps.text: Call 911. Give the exact location.
steps.tl: Tumawag sa 911. Sabihin ang eksaktong lokasyon.
steps.why: saves responders minutes finding you.

steps.text: Do not move them unless there is fire or traffic danger.
steps.tl: Huwag siyang galawin maliban kung may sunog o panganib ng sasakyan.
steps.why: movement can worsen a spinal injury.

steps.text: Do not remove a motorbike helmet.
steps.tl: Huwag tanggalin ang helmet ng motor.
steps.why: removing it can twist the neck.

steps.text: Kneel behind their head. Hold it still.
steps.tl: Lumuhod sa likod ng ulo niya. Hawakan itong hindi gumagalaw.
steps.why: keeps the spine in line.

steps.text: Check breathing.
steps.tl: Tingnan kung humihinga.
steps.why: no breathing = CPR beats everything else.

steps.text: Stop any heavy bleeding.
steps.tl: Pigilan ang malakas na pagdurugo.
steps.why: after breathing, heavy bleeding is the fastest killer.

steps.text: Keep them warm. Keep talking to them.
steps.tl: Panatilihing mainit. Kausapin siya palagi.
steps.why: fights shock and tracks consciousness.

cards.title: Fractures and sprains
signs: deformity, severe pain, can't move it, bone visible, swelling.
doNot: Do NOT straighten it.
Do NOT push it back in.
detail: Fracture signs: deformity, severe pain, can't move it, bone visible, swelling.
1. Do NOT straighten it. Support it in the position found.
2. Bone showing? Cover with clean cloth, press AROUND it, not on it.
3. SPLINT using stiff items, padded, covering the joint above AND below:
magazine, newspaper roll, cardboard, umbrella, stick, ruler, pillow, or tie leg to the other leg / arm to the body.
4. Tie with shirt strips, belt, tape. Snug, not tight; check fingers/toes stay warm and pink.
5. Arm sling: shirt, scarf, or pin the shirt bottom up over the arm.
6. Sprain: Rest, Ice (wrapped, 15–20 min), Compress (cloth wrap), Elevate.
7. Suspect spine/neck/hip/thigh fracture? Don't move them. Call 911.
Dislocation (joint out of place): support it as found. Do NOT push it back in. Sling or padding, cold pack in cloth, see a doctor.
Nearby items: magazine, cardboard, umbrella, stick, belt, shirt, scarf, cold drink can/ice in cloth.
Sources: AHA/Red Cross First Aid Guidelines 2024; ERC Guidelines 2025 First Aid.

steps.text: Do not straighten the limb.
steps.tl: Huwag ituwid ang braso o binti.
steps.why: bone ends can cut vessels and nerves.

steps.text: Bone showing? Cover it. Press around, not on it.
steps.tl: May lumabas na buto? Takpan. Diinan ang paligid, hindi ang buto.
steps.why: lowers infection risk.

steps.text: Splint it with something stiff: magazine, cardboard, or umbrella.
steps.tl: Lagyan ng splint: magasin, karton, o payong.
steps.why: stopping movement reduces pain and damage.

steps.text: Cover the joint above and below.
steps.tl: Takpan ang kasukasuan sa itaas at ibaba.
steps.why: otherwise the broken bone still moves.

steps.text: Tie it with cloth or a belt. Snug, not tight.
steps.tl: Itali ng tela o sinturon. Mahigpit pero hindi masikip.
steps.why: swelling can cut off blood flow.

steps.text: Check fingers or toes stay warm and pink.
steps.tl: Tingnan kung mainit at rosas pa ang daliri.
steps.why: pale or cold means too tight.

steps.text: Arm injury? Make a sling from a shirt or scarf.
steps.tl: Sa braso? Gumawa ng sling mula sa damit o panyo.
steps.why: holds the arm still and takes its weight off the injury.

steps.text: Sprain? Rest, cold pack, wrap, and raise it.
steps.tl: Pilay? Ipahinga, lagyan ng malamig, balutin, at itaas.
steps.why: reduces swelling and pain.

steps.text: Neck, back, or hip injury? Do not move them.
steps.tl: Leeg, likod, o balakang? Huwag siyang galawin.
steps.why: moving can cause paralysis or heavy internal bleeding.

cards.title: Burns
doNot: Don't pull off clothing stuck to skin.

detail: Can cough or talk? Encourage coughing, stay with them.
Can't breathe, cough or speak (hands on throat):
1. Ask "Choking ka?" and tell them you'll help. Call 911.
2. 5 BACK BLOWS: lean them forward, hit hard between shoulder blades with heel of hand.
3. 5 ABDOMINAL THRUSTS: stand behind, fist just above belly button, other hand over it, pull sharply in and up.
4. Repeat 5 + 5 until object comes out or they collapse.
5. Pregnant or very large person: chest thrusts (hands on center of chest) instead of belly.
6. Collapses? Lower to ground, start CPR (card 10). Look in mouth before breaths; remove only what you can see.
Alone and choking? Thrust your belly against a chair back or table edge.
Child 1 yr and up: same as adult, 5 back blows + 5 abdominal thrusts (kneel to their height).
Baby under 1 yr: face-down on your forearm, head low, 5 back blows; flip face-up, 5 chest thrusts with the heel of one hand on the center of the chest. Repeat until it comes out.
Do NOT: hit the back of someone who is still coughing well, give water, do blind finger sweeps, or give belly thrusts to a baby.

steps.text: Can't breathe or speak? Say you will help.

steps.why: a calm patient who knows what's coming cooperates better.

steps.text: Lean them forward.
steps.tl: Iyuko siya nang pasulong.
steps.why: gravity helps the object come out, not go deeper.

steps.text: Give five hard back blows between the shoulder blades.
steps.tl: Limang malakas na palo sa pagitan ng balikat.
steps.why: sharp force can dislodge the object.

steps.text: Stand behind. Fist just above the belly button.
steps.tl: Pumuwesto sa likod. Kamao sa itaas ng pusod.
steps.why: push air up from the lungs to pop the object out.

steps.text: Give five sharp thrusts in and up.
steps.tl: Limang mabilis na tulak papasok at pataas.
steps.why: push air up from the lungs to pop the object out.

steps.text: Repeat back blows and thrusts until it comes out.
steps.tl: Ulitin ang palo at tulak hanggang lumabas.
steps.why: each round can loosen it a little more.

steps.text: Pregnant or large person? Push on the chest instead.
steps.tl: Buntis o malaki ang katawan? Sa dibdib itulak.
steps.why: belly thrusts can harm the baby or won't reach.

steps.text: They collapse? Lower them down. Start CPR.
steps.tl: Bumagsak siya? Ihiga. Simulan ang CPR.
steps.why: compressions also push on the blockage.

steps.text: Baby under one? Five back blows, five chest thrusts, heel of hand.
steps.tl: Sanggol? Limang palo sa likod, limang diin sa dibdib gamit ang palad.
steps.why: heel of one hand gives enough force; belly thrusts can hurt a baby's organs.

detail: HEAT STROKE (EMERGENCY): confused, slurred speech, collapse, seizure, very hot skin (dry OR sweaty).
1. Call 911.

2. COOL FAST: put them in cold water up to the neck (tub, water drum, inflatable pool). No tub? Wrap them in a tarp or plastic sheet with ice water. Otherwise soak with cold water, fan hard, ice or cold cans in cloth at neck, armpits, groin. Keep cooling about 15 minutes or until they are alert.

cards.title: Cardiac arrest (CPR)
nearby: cloth to wipe the chest dry for AED pads
doNot: Don't stop until help takes over or they breathe.
Do NOT: do CPR on a bed or sofa (move them to the floor), stop pushing to check for a pulse, or lean on the chest between pushes.
detail: 1. Tap and shout. No response and not breathing normally (or only gasping)?
2. Call 911, put phone on speaker. Send someone to find an AED (malls, airports, offices).
3. HANDS-ONLY CPR: heel of hand center of chest, other hand on top, arms straight.
- Push hard: 5–6 cm deep, fast: 100–120 per minute (beat of "Stayin' Alive").
- Let chest fully rise between pushes.
4. Trained and willing? 30 pushes then 2 breaths. Not trained? Just push nonstop.
5. AED arrives: turn on and follow voice. Keep pushing until it says stop.
6. Swap pushers every 2 minutes if possible. Don't stop until help takes over or they breathe.
APP: add a 110 bpm metronome beep + vibration on this card.
Do NOT: do CPR on a bed or sofa (move them to the floor), stop pushing to check for a pulse, or lean on the chest between pushes.
Nearby items: phone on speaker, firm floor, AED (mall, airport, office, terminal), jacket to kneel on, cloth to wipe the chest dry for AED pads.

steps.why: confirms they truly can't respond before you start.

steps.text: Not breathing, or only gasping?

steps.why: it's a sign the heart has stopped.

steps.text: Call 911. Put the phone on speaker.
steps.tl: Tumawag sa 911. I-speaker ang telepono.
steps.why: dispatcher can coach you while your hands work.

steps.text: Send someone to find an AED.
steps.tl: Magpahanap ng AED.
steps.why: a shock can restart a heart in a deadly rhythm.

steps.text: Heel of hand on the center of the chest.
steps.tl: Palad sa gitna ng dibdib.
steps.why: pushes directly on the heart.

steps.text: Other hand on top. Arms straight.
steps.tl: Ipatong ang isa pang kamay. Tuwid ang braso.
steps.why: your body weight does the work, so you tire less.

steps.text: Push hard and fast. Follow the beat.
steps.tl: Diinan nang malakas at mabilis. Sundan ang tunog.
steps.why: shallow pushes don't move enough blood.

steps.text: Let the chest come back up each time.
steps.tl: Hayaang umangat ang dibdib bawat diin.
steps.why: the heart refills with blood between pushes.

steps.text: Don't stop until help arrives or they breathe.
steps.tl: Huwag tumigil hanggang dumating ang tulong o huminga siya.
steps.why: every pause drops blood flow to the brain.

steps.text: AED here? Turn it on and follow its voice.
steps.tl: May AED na? Buksan at sundin ang boses nito.
steps.why: a shock can restart a heart in a deadly rhythm.

steps.text: Kneel beside them.

steps.why: keeps the airway open and lets vomit drain.

steps.text: Tilt their head back slightly.

steps.why: stops the tongue blocking the throat.
